clue.text: Stamps out, leaving company to pay for this?

definitions.text: Stamps out, leaving company to pay for this?

parts.words: Stamps out, leaving company to pay for this?
parts.note: read 'stamps out' as 'no stamps needed': a business-reply system where the sender sticks on nothing and the receiving firm pays the postage

explanation.surface: Someone stamping out a fire or a protest, leaving a firm with the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stamps out' looks like crushing something underfoot; here it means postage stamps are left out, because the company receiving the letter pays.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply service where the receiving business covers postage, so the sender needs no stamp at all.

clue.text: One left to put in appearance, so glib

indicators.note: to put in means to insert, so the two letters go inside the other word

parts.note: face means outward appearance, as in on the face of it
one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone leaving just to show their face, which is shallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearance' is the facial sense, as in 'on the face of it'; 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Facile describes something superficial and too easily said, just like glib talk.

clue.text: Taken in by each trap set up

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a net is a trap

explanation.surface: Being caught out by every trap that was laid.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set up' means read upwards; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaten means consumed, taken in as food.

clue.text: Group closing ranks, seeing hard man in GIs' shop

indicators.note: in means placed inside the shop letters

parts.note: a PX is a post exchange, the US military store
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
Alan is a man's name

explanation.surface: A tough guy in an army store sees soldiers close ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: GIs are American soldiers, whose camp store is the post exchange; 'seeing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A phalanx is a tightly massed body of troops or people standing shoulder to shoulder.

clue.text: Subtle change comes over one buying underwear

indicators.note: comes over means goes round, so the shuffled letters surround the other word
change means alter, so the letters of subtle are rearranged

parts.note: a spender is one who buys

explanation.surface: A slight change of heart overtakes a shopper choosing lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subtle change' reads as a slight shift, but 'change' is the anagram signal and 'comes over' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender belt is a women's undergarment that holds up stockings.

clue.text: Agitatedly tuts about doctor, being extreme

indicators.note: about means going round, so the shuffled letters are placed around the doctor
agitated letters are stirred up, so the word tuts is to be rearranged

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: Someone tutting crossly over their doctor, going to extremes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitatedly' makes UTST, and 'about' splits it either side of the doctor; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Utmost as an adjective means of the greatest or most extreme degree.

clue.text: Article on Florida perhaps featuring classic hero

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: the is the definite article
Florida is an example of a state in the SE (south-east) US

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about Florida starring an ancient Greek hero.
explanation.walkthrough: Florida is in the south-east of the United States, SE US; 'featuring' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus is the hero of Greek myth who slew the Minotaur.

clue.text: Old copper on trial's at fault — has he turned a blind eye?

definitions.text: has he turned a blind eye?

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: at fault means wrong, so the letters of trial's are put out of order

parts.note: the letters of trial's, S included

explanation.surface: A former policeman in court is blamed for looking the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned a blind eye' is the idiom for ignoring wrongdoing; here it means made an artificial eye. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocularist is a craftsman who makes artificial eyes, so he literally fashions a blind eye.

clue.text: Being accepted, go up to college, studying geometry?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: being accepted means taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a college

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: A student is admitted and heads off to college to read geometry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses GO to OG; 'go up to college' poses as a student's progress. A polytechnic was a British college of higher education.
explanation.definitionFit: Topology is a branch of mathematics akin to geometry, concerned with properties preserved under stretching.

clue.text: Release pet — one's being kept in is almost cruel

parts.note: a cat is a typical household pet

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is left off
being kept in means held inside another word, here the synonym for cruel

parts.note: harsh means cruel
one is I, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: Freeing a pet because keeping it shut in seems nearly cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being kept in' makes HARSISH; 'almost' then drops its last letter. The word 'is' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Catharsis is an emotional purging or release of pent-up feeling.

clue.text: One supporting slip, maybe, staunchly takes on catch

parts.note: to shoulder a burden is to take it on stoutly
a trap is a catch

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder in the slips, stoutly taking a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' suggests the cricket fielding position; here it is a petticoat, held up by the strap.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoulder strap holds up a garment such as a slip, a woman's undergarment.

clue.text: Provide what's needed in a fit of pique

indicators.note: a fit is a convulsion, so the letters of pique are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Kitting someone out while in a sulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a fit of pique' reads as a temper tantrum; 'fit of' is the anagram signal on PIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to supply them with the gear or means they require.

clue.text: Leaking out where the join is

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of leaking are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pipe dripping at the joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaking out' reads as a drip at a seam; 'out' is the anagram signal on LEAKING.
explanation.definitionFit: A linkage is a connection or joint between parts, the point where things are joined.

clue.text: In general, working clothes may lack finish

indicators.note: lacking a finish means the final letter is removed

parts.note: overalls are protective garments worn for work

explanation.surface: Generally speaking, work wear can look unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may lack finish' strips the last letter, S, from OVERALLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall as an adverb means taken as a whole, generally.

clue.text: Glibness? It has good and bad points

definitions.text: It has good and bad points

parts.note: the word glibness has exactly the letters of blessing, so it is blessing in a mixed order

explanation.surface: Is smooth talk a good thing or a bad thing?
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, 'mix up BLESSING', and you get GLIBNESS, the clue's first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed blessing is something with both advantages and drawbacks.

clue.text: Liquid refreshment stimulating one's palate?

parts.note: liquid refreshment usually means a drink; here it is a rinse that freshens the mouth rather than something swallowed

explanation.surface: A drink that pleases the taste buds.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an antiseptic rinse used to freshen the mouth, refreshing it without being drunk.

clue.text: Make hasty moves to keep communication secret

definitions.meaning: to ... a signal is to encode it so eavesdroppers cannot understand it

explanation.surface: Rushing about to keep a message private.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: hurrying awkwardly, and garbling a transmission so it cannot be intercepted.

clue.text: The balance in the bar perhaps linger, chatting

parts.note: a counter in a pub or shop is an example of a bar

indicators.note: chatting means speaking, so the word is taken as it is said, not spelt

parts.note: to linger is to wait

explanation.surface: Someone at the bar staying on to talk, which balances things out.
explanation.walkthrough: The bar is a pub counter, not a weight bar; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterweight is a mass that offsets another, providing balance.

clue.text: Pioneer with time to talk about saboteur

indicators.note: to talk about means the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a wrecker is one who sabotages

explanation.surface: An explorer pauses to discuss a saboteur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to talk about' says WRECKER is heard, written REKKER, after T; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Trekkers were the Boer pioneers of the Great Trek, and a trekker is any long-distance traveller.

clue.text: Tradesman who may give you a pain, thinking aloud

definitions.text: Tradesman who may give you a pain, thinking aloud

parts.words: Tradesman who may give you a pain, thinking aloud
parts.note: said aloud, a pain sounds like a pane, a sheet of window glass a tradesman fits

explanation.surface: An irritating workman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thinking aloud' tells you 'pain' is to be heard as the glass sheet in a window.
explanation.definitionFit: He fits panes of glass into windows, the tradesman who supplies a pane.

clue.text: Old record in OT book mentioned patriarch

indicators.note: in means placed inside the book abbreviation

parts.note: Josh is the abbreviation for Joshua, a book of the Old Testament
an EP, extended play, is an old record format

explanation.surface: A vintage disc found in an Old Testament book naming a patriarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Testament books have standard short forms; 'mentioned' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph, son of Jacob, is one of the Hebrew patriarchs of Genesis.

clue.text: Get a letter from Greece the day before

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
eve is the day before an event, as in Christmas Eve

explanation.surface: Receiving a letter from Greece the previous day.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve is to get or attain something through effort.

clue.text: Indifferent and 'intrusive annoying individual

indicators.note: intrusive means pushing in, so the word and goes inside the other piece

parts.note: so-so means mediocre, indifferent

explanation.surface: Describing a person who is mediocre and also nosy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intrusive' looks like a description of the person but signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: So-and-so is a mild euphemism for an irritating or disliked person.

clue.text: A wee drop before the play?

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky, a wee drop in Scots

explanation.surface: A small whisky before the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' is a link; the pieces are written DRAM then A.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama means a play for the stage.

clue.text: Rely on keeping large amount of space empty

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the abbreviation sits within the other word

parts.note: to bank on something is to rely on it
L stands for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Counting on holding a lot of room vacant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts L inside BANK; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank is an unfilled gap, a space left vacant on a page or form.

clue.text: Finalise form of wording in a note

parts.note: a term is a word or expression, a particular piece of wording
te is a note in tonic sol-fa

explanation.surface: Settling the wording of a short memo.
explanation.definitionFit: To terminate is to bring to an end, to conclude.

clue.text: Give great encouragement to Sussex horticultural show

indicators.note: show means display, so the letters are on view inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A flower show in Sussex cheering on its exhibitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' looks like part of 'horticultural show' but signals the run inside susSEX HORTicultural.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhort is to urge strongly or encourage earnestly.

clue.text: Expert in Amerindian lore finally rejected proposal

indicators.note: rejected means thrown out, so that letter is removed
in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: Apache is a Native American people
a pro is a professional, an expert

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word lore

explanation.surface: A specialist in Native American tradition turns down an offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally rejected' removes E, the last letter of 'lore', from the tribe's name once the expert is inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An approach can be an overture or proposal made to someone.
